method: Current official Church, eparchy, mission, patriarchal, and Czech Ministry of Culture sources establish published rows. The Prague Eparchy site is currently compromised by unrelated casino content and its parish page conflicts with the live state register, so the current active legal register is used for Prague parish-community existence and the eparchy page only for reconciliation. Search engines, maps, civil associations, media, and independent directories were used only for discovery. Unclear, historical, erased, conflicting, and outside-scope bodies remain here rather than being silently merged or published. Overlapping canonical jurisdictions are preserved neutrally.

candidates.name: St Catherine of Alexandria Orthodox Church in Milovice
candidates.status: hold for current parent roster reconciliation
candidates.reason: The Prague Eparchy parish page names the Milovice church, while the live state register shows the same historic legal identifier under the Brandys nad Labem-Stara Boleslav parish title. Current evidence does not establish whether Milovice is a separate body, a worship site of Brandys, or the current name of that legal parish.

candidates.name: Sts Wenceslas and Ludmila Monastery in Lodenice
candidates.status: hold for current first-party monastery roster
candidates.reason: Current reporting quotes the Prague Eparchy as claiming the monastery and resuming services in 2026, but the official statement was not available on an accessible current eparchial roster and the institution remains in a live civil dispute.

candidates.name: Transfiguration Monastery in Tesov
candidates.status: hold for current first-party monastery confirmation
candidates.reason: A current Czech Orthodox portal identifies the monastery, but no current official Prague Eparchy monastery roster or direct monastery page was located.

candidates.name: St Procopius of Sazava Monastery in Most
candidates.status: hold for current first-party monastery confirmation
candidates.reason: Official Church publications establish the monastery historically, but no current Prague Eparchy monastery roster or current monastery site was located.

candidates.name: St Ludmila of Bohemia Church at the Russian Embassy in Prague
candidates.reason: Moscow official sources establish the church and document it through 2018. Current 2025 and 2026 official reports identify the same priest as rector of the St George Embassy Church instead, and no current separate St Ludmila service or roster record was located.

candidates.name: St Nicholas of Myra Bulgarian Orthodox Church Community in Prague
candidates.reason: An official Bulgarian source documents the community in 2010, but it is absent from the complete current diocesan temple directory.

candidates.name: Claimed Patriarchal Stavropegic Monastery of the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos
candidates.status: hold for current official Ecumenical Patriarchate confirmation
candidates.reason: A Czech civil organization uses this title, while the local Church reported that it lacked consent and the body is absent from the current Ecumenical Patriarchate roster of patriarchal and stavropegic monasteries.

reconciliations.result: Published the 58 parish communities not marked erased in the live Czech Ministry of Culture register. The register groups them explicitly as parish communities in the Prague Eparchy. The compromised eparchy parish page is not treated as evidence of current status where it conflicts with the register.

Did not publish the registry entries marked erased: the original As parish, Ceska Lipa, Decin, Drisy, Horovicky, Cheb, Jaromer II, Karlovy Vary, Koclirov, Kryry, Olovi, Podborany, Rokytnice in the Orlicke Mountains, Rovna, and Tepla u Touzim. Some still appear on the stale or compromised eparchy page, which is not enough to establish current status.

reconciliations.scope: Olomouc and Brno Eparchy current schematism
reconciliations.result: Published every distinct current church, chapel, filial community, monastery, and named worship site in Czechia from the schematism updated 5 November 2026. Shared buildings used by distinct parish communities remain distinct rows; separately named chapels at the same complex remain separate sites.

Published under the direct Russian Church parent. A 2025 civil-title report suggested a transfer to the Russian Diocese of Hungary, but the current Hungarian diocesan temple directory does not list Karlovy Vary and no first-party ecclesiastical transfer statement was located.

jurisdiction_audits.result: No separate Czech body. The official Western European Vicariate document states that the UOC does not open its own parishes in Czechia; clergy serving local structures are not duplicated.
No separately governed Romanian body. Romanian Patriarchate sources state that the Romanian-language Prague parish belongs canonically to the local Church under the Archbishop of Prague.
